doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Benny Carter introduces him to Quincy Jones
summary: Benny Carter kept asking if he knew Quincy Jones, then seated them together; they talked Lucky Thompson, the Hampton band and Clifford Brown.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Oh I’m very flattered. I was introduced to him by Benny Carter who I used to spend every Thursday with when I was in Los Angeles. And he kept saying to me, “Do you know Quincy Jones?” And I went I know who he is but I don’t know him. And the following week he’d say, “Do you know Quincy Jones?” And I thought you know I’ve got to make allowances, he’s 90 something and getting on and maybe he doesn’t remember what I said last time. Then he had a birthday party and he sat me next to Quincy Jones so I knew there was a method in his madness.

I’m trying to imagine what you and Quincy Jones would talk about. I had made an assumption early on in this project that musicians when they get together always talk about music. And then I overheard a conversation once with Frank Wess and Joe Williams and a number of other fellas like that and they weren’t talking about music at all.

Yeah. Well funny enough the great thing about talking with Quincy was I happened to mention Lucky Thompson straight off the bat which of course set him off. And all he wanted to talk about was the Lionel Hampton band and Clifford Brown and Jimmy Cleveland and it was, I’m sure everybody else at the table, I mean it was a big event. And we talked the whole evening. And I don’t think we got any later than 1956. And it was wonderful you know because I suppose nobody ever spoke to him about that anymore you know it was always Michael Jackson or “Off the Wall” or one of those sort of events. So to go back and have somebody mention Lucky Thompson and Clifford Brown and Gigi Gryce was quite a shock I think.
